groups.title: Islands Architecture
groups.question: Your Astro page has a static article, a like button and a comments widget below the fold. Explain how islands make only the interactive parts load JavaScript.

followUps.Client Directives: What do client:load, client:idle and client:visible do?
followUps.Island Isolation and Props Serialization: Why must props passed to islands be serialisable?

evidence.text: client:load hydrates the component immediately.
client:idle waits until the browser is idle.
client:visible hydrates only when the component scrolls into view.
Each island hydrates on its own with its own JavaScript.
Props are embedded in the HTML as data.
So they must be JSON-serialisable; functions cannot be passed.

groups.title: React Integration
groups.question: You added a React counter to an Astro page, but clicking it does nothing. Explain how React works inside Astro.

followUps.Adding the React Integration: What does the React integration add?
followUps.Server-Side vs Client-Side React: Why doesn't the React counter respond to clicks?

evidence.text: The React integration adds React rendering to Astro's build.
It lets you use .jsx and .tsx components.
Without it, React components cannot be rendered.
React components without a client directive render to static HTML only.
No hooks, state or event handlers run in the browser.
Adding a client directive hydrates it so it becomes interactive.

groups.title: Interactivity Patterns
groups.question: A cart icon in the header and an add-to-cart button in the page are separate islands but must share state. Explain how you would connect them and add small scripts.

followUps.Nano Stores for Shared State: How do Nano Stores share state between islands?
followUps.Script Tags and Client-Side JS: How are script tags in Astro components handled?

evidence.text: Nano Stores holds state in small observable stores.
Islands built with different frameworks can subscribe to the same store.
Updating the store updates every island using it.

notEnough: Only saying you use a store.

evidence.text: Scripts are bundled and processed by the build.
A script used in many components ships only once.
is:inline opts out of this processing when needed.

notEnough: Only saying you add a script tag.

groups.title: Multiple Framework Support
groups.question: Your Astro site uses React and Svelte islands, and a map component crashes during build because it uses window. Explain how frameworks mix and when to skip server rendering.

followUps.Mixing Frameworks in One Project: Can a React component pass children to a Svelte component?

evidence.text: Astro can use several frameworks in one project.
Each framework's components render as separate islands.
Components from different frameworks cannot be nested directly inside each other's render code.

notEnough: Only saying Astro supports many frameworks.

evidence.text: client:only skips server rendering for the component.
It suits components that use browser APIs like window during render.
You must tell it which framework to use, since it is not rendered on the server.

notEnough: Only saying it renders on the client.
